title: Water-heater PI control
physicalPurpose: Combine prompt outlet-temperature correction with stored heater output that removes constant-load error.
principalTechnique: Parallel proportional-integral feedback and bounded one-factor tuning
objective: Keep the proven proportional gain fixed, vary only integral gain in a bounded comparison, and select a PI controller that restores temperature promptly without excessive overshoot, saturation, or actuator movement.

simplifications: The recirculating volume is one well-mixed thermal state.
The constant cold-water load changes the zero-power equilibrium by 3 degC.
The separate 45 degC setpoint is unreachable when the no-load equilibrium is 20 degC and heater power is limited to 100 percent.

baseline.limitation: Biased P retains 1.15 degC changed-load error; integral-only removes that error but has 1.62 degC early-load error, 25.5 s recovery, and 17.38 pp movement.

change.decision: Keep Kp fixed at 8, qualify each Ki candidate, and select Ki 4 by shortest eligible recovery before separately exposing an unreachable setpoint.

disturbances: Cold-water flow increases at 60 s in the normal comparison.
A separate no-load exposure changes SP to the unreachable 45 degC at 60 s.

abortPredicates: PV, requested MV, or applied MV is nonfinite
PV or applied MV leaves its hard limit
safety.restorationMode: Manual with 0% requested and applied heater power
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The PI tuning criteria and selected gains are simulation teaching evidence, not approved physical heater settings.
The unreachable setpoint exposure shall not be performed on physical equipment from this lesson.

video.viewerOutcome: Tune one PI balance experimentally, justify the selected Ki from qualified evidence, and explain why requested and applied heater output separate at an unreachable setpoint.

learning.context: The same one-sided recirculating heater holds 35 degC with 75 percent power while cold-water flow changes.
learning.reason: Lesson 5 retained 1.15 degC offset; Lesson 6 removed it but had 1.62 degC early error and 17.38 pp movement.
theory: The setpoint (SP) is desired outlet temperature, process value (PV) is measured outlet temperature, and error (e) is SP minus PV in degrees Celsius.
The proportional gain (Kp) is requested-output percentage points per degree Celsius of present error.
The integral gain (Ki) is stored-output change in percentage points per degree Celsius-second.
The proportional increment (delta_uP) is caused by change in error; the integral increment (delta_uI) is caused by present error and cycle time.
The requested manipulated variable (MV_requested) is preliminary controller output before limits; the applied manipulated variable (MV_applied) is the bounded heater command.
After those quantities are defined, incremental PI adds delta_uP and delta_uI to the previous output.
The integral time (Ti) is seconds for integral action to accumulate the same output contribution as proportional action under unchanged error; Ti equals Kp divided by Ki.
Increasing Ki can improve recovery but can also increase overshoot, saturation, and actuator movement.
learning.workedPrediction: With unchanged 2 degC error, Kp 8, Ki 4, dt 0.1 s, and previous output 75 percent, delta_uP is 0 pp, delta_uI is 0.8 pp, and the preliminary request is 75.8 percent.
practicalPreparation: Start disabled, establish the measured 75 percent Manual holding output, and qualify 35 degC before Auto.
Keep Kp 8 and change only Ki through 0.5, 2, 4, and 8 under one plant, event, timing, limits, and seed.

A live gain edit is adopted by both diagnostics and Control.PID at the beginning of the next 0.1 s scan without resetting retained state; restore and re-establish the Manual holding condition before each independent candidate.
learning.baseline: Use the frozen gain-8 bias-75 and integral-only Ki-0.5 evidence as explanatory references.
learning.change: Execute the bounded Ki sweep, select by declared criteria, then run a separate unreachable 45 degC exposure.
learning.comparison: Define settling, early and final error, recovery, overshoot, applied movement, saturation, eligibility, ranking, and the physical-evidence boundary before results.
learning.validation: Select Ki 4 with 6.6 s recovery and 0.17 degC overshoot; reject Ki 8 for 0.51 degC overshoot, 0.7 s normal saturation, and 67.79 pp movement.
learning.explanation: P supplies prompt correction, I stores the changed holding output, and excessive Ki keeps changing output while delayed temperature response is arriving.
learning.transfer: Tune one factor at a time on another self-regulating process; Lesson 8 studies the requested/applied mismatch exposed by the separate unreachable setpoint.
